name: tmux new -s
description: Start a new named session.

flags.description: Attach if the session already exists, otherwise create it

examples.description: Create and attach to a session named work
Attach to work, or create it if missing
Run a command in a detached session

notes: `tmux new` is short for `tmux new-session`.

name: tmux ls
description: List running sessions.
notes: Short for `tmux list-sessions`. Inside tmux, Ctrl-b s shows an interactive session tree.

name: tmux attach -t
description: Attach to an existing session.

flags.description: Detach other clients attached to the session

examples.description: Attach to the most recent session
Attach and kick other clients (fixes size issues)

name: Ctrl-b d
description: Detach from the current session, leaving it running in the background.

examples.description: Detach all other clients from this session

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
Processes keep running after detaching, which makes tmux ideal for long jobs over SSH.

name: Ctrl-b $
description: Rename the current session.

examples.description: Rename a session from the shell
Rename the current session from inside tmux

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.

name: tmux kill-session -t
description: Terminate a session and all its windows and processes.

examples.description: Kill every session except the current one
Kill all sessions and the tmux server

notes: WARNING: All programs running in the session are killed and unsaved work is lost.

name: Ctrl-b s
description: Interactively choose a session (and window) to switch to.

examples.description: Switch the current client to another session

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
Ctrl-b ( and Ctrl-b ) cycle to the previous/next session.

name: Ctrl-b c
description: Create a new window in the current session.

examples.description: Open in the current pane's directory

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.

name: Ctrl-b 0..9 / n / p / w
description: Switch windows by number, next/previous, or from a list.

examples.description: Pick from a window list (Ctrl-b w)

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
Ctrl-b l jumps to the last active window.

name: Ctrl-b ,
description: Rename the current window.
notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
Ctrl-b & kills the current window (asks for confirmation); `tmux kill-window -t 2` from the shell.

name: Ctrl-b %
description: Split the current pane into left and right panes.

examples.description: Right pane takes 30% of the width

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
tmux's -h means a horizontal layout (panes side by side), i.e. a vertical divider.

name: Ctrl-b "
description: Split the current pane into top and bottom panes.
notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.

name: Ctrl-b arrow / o / q
description: Move between panes.

examples.description: Move to the pane on the left (Ctrl-b Left); -R, -U, -D for other directions
Show pane numbers, then press a number to jump (Ctrl-b q)

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
Ctrl-b ; toggles to the last active pane. Ctrl-b x kills the current pane; Ctrl-b { / } swaps panes.

name: Ctrl-b Ctrl-arrow
description: Resize the current pane.
notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
Ctrl-b Space cycles through preset layouts. Hold Ctrl after the prefix and tap the arrow repeatedly to keep resizing.

name: Ctrl-b z
description: Toggle the current pane to fill the whole window, and back.
notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
A Z flag appears in the status bar window name while zoomed.

name: setw synchronize-panes
description: Send keyboard input to every pane in the window at once.

examples.description: Turn on (from inside tmux: Ctrl-b : then `setw synchronize-panes on`)

notes: WARNING: Every keystroke goes to all panes; be careful with destructive commands on multiple servers.

name: Ctrl-b [
description: Enter copy mode to scroll back, search, and copy text.
notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
In emacs mode (default) start selection with Ctrl-Space and copy with Alt-w; with `setw -g mode-keys vi` use Space/v and Enter/y. Search with / or ? (vi) or Ctrl-s/Ctrl-r (emacs). q exits.
Ctrl-b PgUp enters copy mode and scrolls up immediately. `set -g mouse on` enables wheel scrolling.

name: tmux send-keys
description: Send keystrokes to a pane, useful for scripting layouts.

examples.command: tmux send-keys -t work:1.0 'npm run dev' Enter
examples.description: Run a command in pane 0 of window 1 of session work
Send Ctrl-C to a session's active pane

notes: Targets use session:window.pane syntax. Key names like Enter, C-c, Escape are sent as keys, not literal text.

name: Ctrl-b :
description: Open the tmux command prompt to run any tmux command.

examples.description: Type at the prompt to enable mouse support for this server
Commands at the prompt omit the leading `tmux`

notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.

name: tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf
description: Reload the tmux configuration without restarting.

examples.description: Add to ~/.tmux.conf to reload with Ctrl-b r

notes: tmux 3.1+ also reads ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf.
Common config lines: `set -g mouse on`, `set -g base-index 1`, `setw -g mode-keys vi`, `set -g prefix C-a`.
Removed settings are not unset by reloading; restart the server (`tmux kill-server`) for a clean state.

name: Ctrl-b ?
description: List all key bindings.
notes: Key bindings shown assume the default prefix Ctrl-b; press the prefix, release, then press the key.
